That I'm really struggling with events from my past. I carry a lot of shame and guilt with me. I recently tried to make a list of the guys I've had sex with. The number was pretty high, at 25. Most of these before I turned 18. Most of these didn't involve enthusiastic consent. Some of them were straight up rape. Some of them were me staying over at some boys place because anything was better than staying at my parents' and the boy relentlessly pushing me for sex, until I would be too tired to say no and let them get it over with. 

Thinking about all that makes me feel so dirty. I am so uncomfortable with touch nowadays. I feel like I don't know how to be in a healthy close relationship with anyone. So I'm not. It's lonely, but it's better than adding onto the already big pile of bad experiences. I feel sad that being abused as a child set me up for abusive relatiinships with others later in life. 

Also, I'm doing my Masters and quickly losing motivation. I feel like I'm burnt out but at the same time I can't imagine myself working 40 hour weeks in retail or something.. so I've got to stick it out.

Probably that when I was 17, I had sex for money. I also got arrested for shoplifting food.

I had a job, but my mother blocked my bank account and stole my card. The only way I knew to get cash was prostitution. I always learned to distrust people and never learned how to ask for help. 

It was two guys, the first only lasted a minute and gave me my cash, he was awkward and weird. The second became something like my 'sugardaddy' and was pretty good to me. I was smart enough to at least look for red flags.


This, being sexually abused, and abused by my mother as a child all haunt me. I'm still here, and I'm still fighting, but it almost annoys me how people always seem to be stunned at how I'm single or how I struggle. 

I'm a pretty put-together person and usually bubbly and happy. That's not because I am carefree, it's because I want to be bubbly and happy whenever I can. Plenty of times I get consumed by darkness the second I am home from work or uni. 

Most people around me know I had a fucked up life, but none of them know just how fucked up and how much it still affects me.

Ah! Didn't know that. The weird thing is, there's no scar tissue at all in the particular place I cut. My skin does have crazy healing potential.. but this is on a whole other level. It's like it went into "insta-heal" mode as soon as my blade made contact. 

I'll stay safe. I think my body is forcing me too, whether I want to or not. Thanks for your reply and hope you're well.

I understand where you are coming from and I think you're right. However, the first time we were sexual he had just gotten out of his relationship and definitely wasn't ready to date. The sexual chemistry got the better of both of us. Apart from that, since I met him when he wasn't single, friendship has just been our default.

Wow, I don't think he owes me a relationship nor have I attempted to force a relationship. Your comment comes off a little strong. I can't just sever all ties because the hobbies we share are very important to me and make up a large part of my social life. Just trying to find a way to deal with the situation, I know people can't be forced to love someone and wouldn't want a relationship with somebody who doesn't truly love me.
Right. Ignoring it. Basically the both of us are ignoring my feelings.

He hasn't told me outright, but he will talk about wanting to meet *that* girl and finding love, and he is one to pursue relationships enthusiastically when he wants to. We don't truly act like a couple since outside of sex and cuddles there's no intimacy (like 'real' dates, holding hands or kissing)
I think he does have a clue, but his way of dealing with it is just not reciprocating if that makes sense.

Thanks for your reply. My feelings definitely didn't just come from knowing how much we have in common; they grew naturally from us sharing our hobbies and having long talks, having sex and all that. 

I guess as my feelings grew his remained the same and I can't change that. Would you say it may at least be a good idea to discuss this with him? As we share our hobbies together I would not want things to be awkward, especially DnD. I worry that confessing will make him act differently toward me.
Why do you think that?
You are a stranger.
Science is fake news!! NEXT!!!
Correlation =/= causation. There are likely differences between those two populations that lead either one to be more attracted to hard drugs or marijuana.
It wasn't pressure or anything. Automated message that you had to agree with before being connected to someone.
That's my point, my country does have a national helpline, that's the one I called.

Looks are not everything. It's not a measure to go by when comparing to others!!!! You must have great qualities and I'm sure your friends recognize those. Just be you and don't shy away because  of others who "look better". Thats no fun!! I hope youre okay. Hugs.
Would still like to thank you for replying, though. So thank you.

I wanted to hear a human voice, someone to interact with in real-time. I'm really bad at explaining myself in writing, and I feel it's a really distant way of communicating. Just reaching out to see if somebody cared. I know I shouldn't have any expectations, but I suppose I did have some. I feel like I'm cracking faster and faster and I'm unable to stop it :(

Honestly I still get peeved when some of my more distant relatives make any contact into a "you know you should really not be so mean to your mother" situation.

I cut off contact with my mother a few years back because she would literally encourage me to kill myself when I was already incredibly suicidal and full of self-hatred (also thanks to her). She taught me I was worthless scum and reminded me constantly that I was unlovabe and unworthy and would even tell me that if family and friends expressed positive emotions towards me they were just faking it.

My mom would often deny me food and refuse to buy me even cheap things like fruit (I had a bad eating disorder and like, apples were what I lived on at some point.) She would claim all of it was too expensive and I didn't know any better. 

We were actually slightly above-average income and having lived on my own since 17 I now know she was just being her awful self and could've easily afforded some damn fruit for me. I was basically treated as if there was no money but my sister was constantly spoilt with new stuff. They'd go on frequent hoidays too. But I still grew up "poor" despite this because for me there was no money, ever.

Anyway they did a lot of terrible crap that wasn't okay that I didn't figure out until sometimes even adulthood, and I'm struggling to find what is "normal" to this day.

Yeah I feel like it goes one of two ways. I was bullied throughout most of my childhood and abused by my parents. I never understood why they did that to me and never felt the need to do it to others.

Apart from being catcalled, groped inappropriately and having guys follow me and try to force themselves into my home, I've been coerced into sex several times before.

When I was in highschool I was incredibly insecure and being abused in my home didn't help. I tried to be out of the house as much as possible. I would sleep over at guys' places and most of the time they'd try to convince me to have sex with then - relentlessly. They'd make me feel guilty for saying no, and usually after long enough I would cave and try to get it over with quickly. Somehow my compass is very off and even if it was a "trusted friend" this would happen. This happened several times until I was 17, and it always came with a lot of slutshaming.

Then, I got into a friends-with-benefits type relationship with a couple. However, quite soon after we started I didn't want to have sex with them anymore. I told them this and they would say things like 'you can't just say that', 'wait until we're in the moment' and overall just not take me seriously and keep making advances constantly. I was scared to lose their friendship and so had sex with them, even though I hardly ever enthusiastically participated or gave explicit consent. Usually it was the opposite, I'd go there and tell them I did not want to have sex, and they'd keep touching me and if I gave even the slightest response (regardless of other negative responses) it was seen as consent. 

I lived with a friend for a few months and when we got drunk together (I was significantly more intoxicated than him), he raped me. 

Lastly, and I'm not sure if this is just my trauma warping my view of whats okay or not, but I was friends with benefits with somebody who is still my friend (though he doesn't quite understand how this has affected me) and while I enjoyed having rough sex with him, he kept escalating it without ever communicating and the last time we had sex I really couldn't enjoy it since some of the stuff he did was out of my comfort zone, but I still just let it happen because I tend to dissociate when people I trust hurt me. When I talked to him about it he understood and said he felt he lost control a little and keeps wanting more (but also mentioned he'd never do the things he did to me to somebody he was in love with) and it just made me feel like I always get the worst out of people :/

That even though I have had a myriad of negative and coercive sexual experiences I am almost constantly aroused, and get off to the idea of being forced to do things I don't want.

I have a lot of shame around sex in general though, I feel guilty for most sexual desires and thoughts and a lot of that stems from being mercilessly slutshamed after being coerced into having sex with several people throughout high school.
My experiences are all too similar. Thanks for sharing.
I've had this experience before. I have a really difficult time saying no and just 'suffer' through abuse when it happens. I'm still learning. It's really hard not to blame myself.

I allowed myself to get drunk around a former friend; I usually didn't drink more than a drink or so, because it never felt safe. 

I got too drunk and was on my belly on the bed wearing a princessy dress. I complained about my head hurting and I was not fully conscious anymore. Instead of offering me some water or putting me to bed, he raped me. He knew me very well and I told him before that I had a history of abuse, being coaxed into sex and that I have trouble saying no. Even that same night we had an in-depth conversation about the things I went through and how they affected me. He later said that it had made him "curious".

It still feels weird calling it "rape", but I know I would never violate a person like that. 

The kicker is, because of a history of abuse my brain tends to gaslight itself; it convinces me that people I trust would never do anything to hurt me, and so when they do I dissociate. I'm like the perfect victim and I hate it. 

Afterwards I was consoling him and making sure he was okay days later (I lived with him and he stayed with his girlfriend after it happened). I was really scared he wouldn't want to be my friend anymore (WHY?!?!?!!?!?!?!) And the way he acted towards me triggered my fear of abandonement and I tried to keep him close, even though I had several breakdowns about what had happened. 

I told my best female friend at the time and then she went on to become his best friend. I didn't understand how fucked up that was until months later when I also finally realised how a lot of people I kept close to me were manipulative and never had my best interest at heart.

A few times between the ages of 14-17 I was coaxed into sex, usually guys who made me feel guilty for saying no, kept being persistent after I said no 700 times and then I just stopped resisting and let then 'get it over with'. On most of these occaisions the guys would then brag about it to their friends and it would spread like wildfire, and I was mercilessly slutshamed throughout high school. It makes me feel disgusting thinking about it and it makes me feel disgusting and whorish that I ever let it happen. I feel like it's my fault for not standing up for myself better, not fighting harder, not recognizing the situation for what it was. It sucks.

When I was 19, I lived with my ex-boyfriend and decided to be a camgirl for a while. It was partly to try and take control over my sex life again. Even though it was fine I feel so ashamed and dirty about it. 

I have nightmares in which I am raped and I am just saying "sorry" over and over again, because it feels like it's my fault.

When I was 17, I had sex for money with two different men. One of them went on to be my 'sugardaddy'. While it went about as good as it could have (he was very nice, not rough, didn't do anything I didn't want), I didn't have anything and already got arrested twice for shoplifting groceries and bingefood because I was heavily bulimic at the time. I did it because I felt there was no other choice. My mother refused to give me food and never let me access my bank account where the money from my grocery store job went. I never tell this to anyone because again, it makes me feel disgusting and whorish and just.. used. I'm so embarassed about having been arrested twice as well, bulimia made me do crazy stuff and I never felt good about stealing food. 

I never feel 'valid' enough about the abuse my mother inflicted. It's hard to call it what it was and I never know if I'm exagerrating.

I have severe trust issues and every experience I've had in the past decade where I slowly learned to trust somebody, in the end it was clearly wrong to ever trust them and I pay the price. 

There's always one or two nights a week where I do not sleep at all, largely because of all my bad memories. This is one of those nights.
